entries.title: Proverbs 22:3
segments: 3. are punished--that is, for their temerity; for the evil is not necessarily punitive, as the prudent might otherwise be its objects.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:4
segments: 4. humility and the fear of the Lord--are in apposition; one produces the other. On the results, compare

entries.title: Proverbs 22:5
segments: 5. he that ... them--Those who properly watch over their own souls are thus preserved from the dangers which attend the way of perverse men (

entries.title: Proverbs 22:6
segments:
6. Train--initiate, or early instruct. 
 
    the way--literally, "his way," that selected for him in which he should go; for early training secures habitual walking in it.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:7
segments: 7. The influence of wealth sets aside moral distinctions is implied, and, of course, disapproved (compare

entries.title: Proverbs 22:8
segments: 8. (Compare

). 
 
    the rod ... fail--His power to do evil will be destroyed.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:9
segments:
9. a bountiful eye--that is, a beneficent disposition. 
 
    for he giveth ... poor--His acts prove it.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:10
segments: 10. Cast out--or drive away. Scorners foster strife by taunts and revilings.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:11
segments:
11. (Compare Margin). 
 
    pureness of heart--and gentle, kind words win favor, even from kings.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:12
segments:
12. preserve--or guard. 
 
    knowledge--its principles and possessors. 
 
    overthroweth--utterly confounds and destroys the wicked.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:13
segments: 13. Frivolous excuses satisfy the indolent man's conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:14
segments: 14. The mouth--or flattering speeches (
) ensnare man, as pits, beasts. God makes their own sin their punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:15
segments: 15. is bound--or firmly fixed. Chastisement deters from crime and so leads to reformation of principle.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:16
segments: 16. These two vices pertain to the same selfish feeling. Both are deservedly odious to God and incur punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:17
segments: 17. Here begins another division of the book, marked by those encouragements to the pursuit of wisdom, which are found in the earlier chapters. It will be observed that at
, the proverbs are generally expressed in two verses instead of one (see (unresolved link)).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:18
segments:
18. These lessons must be laid up in the mind, and 
 
    fitted--or better, "fixed" in the lips so as to be ever ready.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:19
segments: 19. That ... Lord--This is the design of the instruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:20
segments:
20. excellent things--or probably of former times. 
 
    counsels and knowledge--both advice and instruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:21
segments: 21. Specially he desires to secure accuracy, so that his pupil may teach others.
